P.C.:-
1.
Heard Ms. Ranjita Barhate, learned Advocate for the Applicant and Mr. K. K. Naik, learned APP for Respondent-State.
2. This proceeding is listed for the first time today.
Issue Notice to the Respondent.
Mr. K. K. Naik, learned APP waives service for Respondent-State.
3. The Applicant has filed this Anticipatory Bail Application as he apprehends arrest.

The FIR is registered on 22 October 2024 at 17.13 hours in C.R. No.0427 of 2024, under Sections 123, 223, 274,
275 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 ("BNS") read with Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(ii), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(e) and 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 with Pachod Police Station, District Ch.
Sambhajinagar.

sentences.text: 1 4. Heard learned Advocate for the parties and with their assistance, I have perused the FIR and the record available with the record.
The Informant is one-Pragya Pramod Surase, aged 36 years.
At the very outset, learned Advocate for the Applicant would submit that the alleged crime in the present matter relates to a banned substance i.e. Gutkha.
The perusal of the FIR would reveal that the Applicant is the supplier of the said contraband, such contraband which has been duly seized.
There is no recovery to be effected.

Mr.
Naik would not controvert such factual position.
Such recovery has been effected from the shop of the co-accused person, who according to the learned Advocate for the Applicant has been released on regular bail from the Trial Court.
The name of the Accused person initially was not mentioned in the FIR.
It was subsequently revealed from the statement of co-accused during investigation.
The Applicant has no criminal antecedents as pointed out by learned Advocate for the Applicant.

5. Ms. Barhate, learned Advocate for the Applicant would draw the attention of the Court to an order dated 23 July 2025 in Anticipatory Bail Application No.1248 of 2025, where the Applicant similarly placed has been protected by interim order of this Court.

Such protection was on the basis of order passed in Anticipatory Bail Application No.857 of 2025 and connected proceedings concerning the  3 of 4 917-ABA.1401.2025 Akhatar Karim Shaikh vs The State Of Maharashtra on 13 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18377049/
2 said contraband i.e. Gutkha.
6. Considering the above, at this stage, in my view, the Applicant deserve some protection by passing the following order:
 ORDER (i) Until adjourned date of hearing, in the event of arrest of the Applicant in connection with C.R.
No.0427 of 2024 dated 22 October 2024, registered with Pachod Police Station, District Ch.
Sambhajinagar for the offences punishable under Sections 123, 223, 274, 275 of BNS read with Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(ii), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)
(e) and 30(2)(a) of the food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Applicant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing PR bond in the sum of Rs.20,000 (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or more sureties in the like amount.
